abstract: We establish two positivity regimes for generalized Laguerre expressions of Hardy's function and the completed Riemann xi-function at orders proportional to logarithmic height. If $c=2p/\log(t/(2\pi))$ stays in a fixed compact subinterval of $(1/2,\infty)$, we prove a uniform pointwise asymptotic with leading term $2\log(t/(2\pi))^{2p}|\zeta(1/2+c+it)|^2/(2p)!$ for Hardy's function. The completed xi-function has the corresponding positive gamma normalization. A pair of real Cauchy saddles supplies the main term; absolute convergence controls its amplitude, and convexity makes the complementary arcs smaller. For fixed $0<\theta<\alpha<1/2$, we also prove positivity of smooth long averages at $2p+1\sim\alpha\log T$, against every nonzero Dirichlet polynomial of length at most $T^\theta$, uniformly in arbitrary complex coefficients. An exact divisor-incidence generator gives a relative holomorphic bound for gcd matrices around the positive saddle. A complete two-factor approximate functional equation on a fixed shift disk retains both main terms, cancels the extra residues, and controls growing-order coefficient extraction without hidden factorial losses. These contributions differ from fixed-derivative sign proportions and from Laguerre inequalities for shifted Maclaurin sequences. Two reproducible finite controls check coefficient identities independently; the uniform conclusions rest on the analytic proofs. An explicit concentration bound shows why the arithmetic mean does not supply a direct microscopic witness. Low-order pointwise inequalities, zero-density improvements, and the Riemann hypothesis remain unresolved.
author: bramble_trace
title: Laguerre positivity at logarithmic order: pointwise and arithmetic mean theorems
